claims.reason: After the per-graph bound `hcond`, both proofs run the same averaging argument. It is `expect_mono_support`, then the `simp_rw` expectation lemmas, then `hy` from `localSet_mass` and `mass_mono`, then `D.drift`, then the `localSet_mass`/`localSet_cost` rewrites. It then uses `B_le_one` to weaken `B x*g*V + 12ζV` to `(g+12ζ)V` (`hVB`, `nlinarith`), multiplies by `h`, and closes with `linarith`. The shared steps match line for line. The differences are `μ` versus `μ.real`, `s.2 j` versus `S`, and `client j` versus `client`. The hypotheses (`hg hunit hP hP1 hx0 hx1 hζ0 hζ1 he hfirst hpair`, `hactive`, `hS`, `hm₀`) are the same. The averaging block is about 15 lines of real reasoning, not a short calculation. The two theorems differ only in the `hcond` proof and the final law-coercion step, so the helper does not just move a branch. The helper can live in PhysicalState.lean, which RationalPhysicalDrift already imports, so no dependency cycle arises. A fix to the constants, such as the `B ≤ 1` weakening, currently has to be made in both places.
claims.shared_lemma:
theorem graph_average_drift {F : Type*} [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {Δ : ℕ} {g P x h ζ c₀ f : ℝ} (s : Finset (Copy (F := F) Δ)) (S S₀ : Finset (Copy (F := F) Δ)) (location : F → X) (client : X) (D : Taper.GraphData Δ g P (fun i : s => location i.val.1) (own Δ s)) (μ : FiniteLaw (s → Finset s)) (E : (s → Finset s) → ℝ) (hg : 0 < g) (hunit : g*(Δ:ℝ)=1) (hP0 : 0 ≤ P) (hP1 : P ≤ 1/2) (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) (hh0 : 0 ≤ h) (hζ0 : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζ1 : ζ < 1/4) (he : |P - Analytic.P x| ≤ ζ) (hfirst : ∀ a i, μ.expect (fun G => GraphLaw.edge G a i) = D.marginal a i) (hpair : ∀ a b i j, i ≠ j → μ.expect (fun G => GraphLaw.edge G a i * GraphLaw.edge G b j) = D.marginal a i * D.marginal b j) (hactive : S ⊆ s) (hS : S ⊆ S₀) (hm₀ : mass g S₀ = 1) (b : F → ℝ) (hcond : ∀ G, 0 < μ.weight G → E G ≤ f + h*(timeRate x (mass g S) * PhysicalPotential.cost g (fun i => dist client (location i.1)) S + g * ∑ e ∈ relevant (graphActions G) (localSet s S), charge (graphActions G) x g b (fun i => dist client (location i.val.1)) (localSet s S) e) + c₀) : μ.expect E ≤ f + h*(g+12*ζ)*PhysicalPotential.cost g (fun i => dist client (location i.1)) S + c₀
(b should have the same type as in D.drift, i.e. the cap function on the active copies, not necessarily F → ℝ.) Proof sketch: apply expect_mono_support to hcond and simplify with the expect_add/const/mul lemmas. Get hy from localSet_mass and mass_mono. Apply D.drift and rewrite with localSet_mass/localSet_cost. Weaken B x ≤ 1 to get a + E[chargeSum] ≤ (g+12ζ)V. Multiply by h and close with linarith.
rewritten_uses: CopyState.roundLaw_drift: after `hcond` (the `conditional_round_drift` call, unchanged), `have key := graph_average_drift s.1 (s.2 j) (S₀ j) location (client j) D μ (fun G => (PhysicalBatchLaw.law …).expect (fun Z => statePotential R d (x*Real.exp (-h)) g (advance s G (H G) Z x g d) j)) hg hunit hP0 hP1 hx0 hx1 hh0 hζ0 hζ1 he hfirst hpair (hactive j) (hS j) (hm₀ j) b hcond`. Then `rw [roundLaw, FiniteLaw.expect_bind]; simp_rw [FiniteLaw.expect_map]; exact key`, with the usual `change` for `f`.

RationalPhysicalKernel.step_drift: after `hcond` (the `rational_conditional_round_drift` call, unchanged), `have key := graph_average_drift s.1 S S₀ location client D μ.real (fun G => (ν G).real.expect (v G)) hg hunit hP.le hP1 hx0 hx1 hh0 hζ0 hζ1 he hfirst hpair hactive hS hm₀ b hcond`. Then finish with `rw [step_expectation]; change …; rw [← SparseIntegerLaw.real_expect_all]; simp_rw [hpoint]; exact key`. The `hy`, `hgen`, `hVB`, `hgen'`, `hmul` and `hfinish` blocks disappear.
